questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't have that many preferences as to where I wanted to go, but I knew I wanted to go to the US. The midwest, and especially Wisconsin turned out to really be a great place. This is, from my understanding especially true when coming from Denmark, since there is a lot of scandinavian heritage in the midwest area.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend going to UW-Madison since it is a really nice place to both explore academic opportunities, socialise with other students and explore midwestern America.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was super easy. The university really does a lot for you to feel welcome, and there was even a fair which introduced international students to all the different things on campus.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The university does also send out a lot of emails with useful information once you get here.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy. I used to facebook site "NEW UW Madison Sublet and Roommate Board" to find a room located in the centre of campus.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is mostly 1 and 2-year students who live on-campus (dorms), so if you wanna live a place with more pricavy and with people the same age as you i would recommend off-campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Be aware that off-campus housing is a lot easier to find in the spring since a lot of Americans go abroad themselves.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It can be a bit tricky to choose courses and to know which courses are good, but as long as you look out for emails from the university you should be all good.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Looking up the professors online and seeing what other students thought of them.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: If you take the time and sit down at look properly at it, you should be just fine.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't be afraid that you picked the wrong course. Within the first two weeks, you can change your courses, if you regret choosing one. As long as you report if back to KU.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some of the lower-level courses can seem a bit too easy since people are a bit younger when starting university (18-19). Most of the courses have some really great professors who are really committed to your learning. Be sure to tell them that you're not from the U.S., they will love it.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Most classes are divided into lectures with the professor and discussion sections with a TA (teaching assistant, who is usually a student themselves or recently graduated). You go to the lectures and listen and go to the discussion section and discuss what the professor said.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
EDPSYCH301: How People Learn (003) SP22
FOLKLORE100: Introduction to Folklore (001) SP22
SCANDST432: History of Scandinavia Since 1815 (001) SP22
SLAVIC245: Topics in Slavic Literatures

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Slavic245 is really great if you're interested in post-communism cultures!
SCANDST432 is a really really great course. Basically all courses with professor Dean Krouk.

questions.answer: Food was a bit more expensive, because of the inflation.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are almost 900 different clubs to be a part of! all from cheese tasting to skiing. There is basically a club for everyone.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Be a part of hoffers! It's an outdoor club which does sailing, swimming, hiking etc.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go see "The house on the rock". It's a crazy house outside of the city.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, since the culture is very Western.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Americans are really good at socializing, so just go up to someone and say you're from Denmark and enjoy your new friends!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The food is not that great honestly. You will have a hard time eating healthy. If you like enormous amounts of cheese, you will be in heaven.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Everyone is super helpful and approachable!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be prepared to socialize! Americans love to talk, so don't be worried if you'll make new friends.
Be prepared to do many more small assignments. IF you are used to doing 1-2 big assignments at the end of the semester, you will be surprised. There are many more small assignments and quizzes throughout the semester. This can be tricky, but it makes the exam period a lot less struggling. 
Be open to new things!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend the ScanDesign foundation, which is a fellowship with other Scandinavian students. For me, it was a really big part of the exchange and made sure you also had some fellow Scandinavians to discuss problems with or go to social events together. You will have to apply to be a part of it, and a scholarship also comes along! Look it up online.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding thing was also the most challenging. The progress of being alone and figuring out a lot of things on your own felt really good, and really helps making you a better student and person.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being away from your friends and danish food.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
